enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
1153 AM MDT Sun Oct 18 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...


.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 1130 AM MDT Sun Oct 18 2026

 - Low rain chances through Wednesday, favoring western areas.

 - Better areawide rain chances Thursday and Friday, with some
   strong storms and flooding possible.

 - Warming back to above normal by midweek.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1130 AM MDT Sun Oct 18 2026

The region will remain under a predominantly southwest flow
pattern aloft and low level south to southeast winds. Both will be
bringing some moisture into the region. Currently there is a
weakening upper low that is near San Diego and will be slowly
lifting NE with some subtle disturbances moving out ahead of it.
These little waves will bring on and off showers with a
thunderstorm also possible to areas mainly west of a KALM-KELP
line. Nothing more than low scattered coverage. NBM seemed to
under do the PoPs early on and wanted at least some mention of
precipitation for these areas. Low and high temperatures will be
on the rise with increasing moisture and southerly low level flow.
Highs will be in the mid 70s to mid 80s for the lowlands with lows
remaining in the mainly in the 50s, although a few 40s possible
tonight. 

For Tue-Wed, we will be more in a transitioning period with first
system out of the area but a stronger upper low will be moving
down the CA coast. Besides some light showers out west, drier
conditions return with highs continuing to warm. Upper flow turns
slightly more S than SW and taps better moisture from south of 
the Gulf of CA. As we go into Thu this moisture will meet better
lift over the Borderland ahead of the upper low and we will see
more widespread precipitation developing which could continue into
the weekend. Temperatures will fall back into the 70s. Do not see
any mountain snow chances as the southerly flow keeps mid level
temperatures very mild.  



&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAFS)
Issued at 1130 AM MDT Sun Oct 18 2026

P6SM FEW-SCT070-090 SCT-BKN120-150 to start with increasing SCT-
BKN060-080 BKN120-150 after 00Z and continuing to the end of the 
period. Expect isolated showers to move through eastern terminals
this evening with a better(30%) chance around KDMN. A thunderstorm
can't be ruled out but kept thunder mention out of TAF for now.
Little impact expected from these cells besides some brief gusty
winds.  


&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1130 AM MDT Sun Oct 18 2026

Fire weather concerns will remain low through the period as
moisture returns to the area. A few showers and thunderstorms are
possible, especially western half of the area through early in the
week. A stronger storm system moves into the west later in the
week and will bring more widespread rain to the region.
Temperatures will be warming into the mid 70s to mid 80s through
Wednesday with RH's remaining above 25% with light winds. Cooler
temps and higher RH's for late in the week. Vent rates the next
couple of days will be Poor east to Good west on Mon and 
improving to Good to Very good on Tue. 

&&
